content.text: Not every definition reports how a word is used.

content.definition: Gives a new word, or a new meaning, for a discussion. It is neither true nor false.
Makes a vague word exact for one purpose, such as a law or a study.
Builds a disputed view into a definition, to win an argument.

examples.title: Stipulative
lines: Let 'gorp' mean a mix of nuts and raisins.
examples.note: A new word for our talk. It cannot be wrong, only useful or not.

examples.title: Persuasive
examples.note: This packs a disputed claim into a definition. Watch for definitions built to win an argument.

question.prompt: For tax purposes, a 'dependent' is someone who gets more than half their support from you. What kind of definition is this?
question.hint: Is 'dependent' a new word, or an everyday word made exact for one purpose?
question.explanation: 'Dependent' is a vague everyday word. The tax rule makes it exact for one purpose, so this is a precising definition.
